issues.issue: Can the doctrine of legitimate expectations be relied on to override section 190 of IRPA?
issues.applicant_position: Section 190 applies by its clear terms; legitimate expectations is a procedural doctrine that cannot override Parliament; no duty to forewarn.
issues.respondent_position: Officials should have forewarned her and her husband that pending legislation could affect his status, so the former Act should govern.
issues.result_quote: I would therefore answer the first certified question in the negative.

issues.issue: What does "at the time of that application" in paragraph 117(9)(d) of the Regulations refer to?
issues.applicant_position: The phrase covers the whole life of the application, up to landing at the port of entry, so the undisclosed marriage excludes the husband.
issues.respondent_position: The phrase refers only to when the visa application was filed, when she was unmarried, so the husband is not excluded.
issues.result_quote: the phrase "at the time of that application" in paragraph 117(9)(d) of the Regulations contemplates the life of the application from the time when it is initiated
